title: Close G5-C2: cryptographically bind forwarded prompt content to the operator-named approval digest (owner am.14)
objective: Close the G5-C2 journal-write two-field-forgery residual per owner am.14 (D-010 R134-R143) with exactly ONE narrowly bounded security fix: an attacker who modifies BOTH the parked prompt bytes AND prompt_bytes_digest while leaving the operator-named approval digest unchanged MUST NOT be able to cause altered prompt content to be forwarded; bind the forwarded content cryptographically to information independently covered by the operator-named approval_digest rather than relying solely on mutable journal fields (R136). Preserve the S13.5 timestamp/clock invariant; smallest correct design - e.g. generate the non-authoritative FORWARDED AT stamp only at actual forward time, or persist/recompute the structured approved instruction at approve/resume (R137). Mandatory 7-property adversarial test (R138) + the four also-prove properties (R139). NO supervisor redesign, additional features, new infrastructure, or broader cleanup (R140).
business_reason: Owner am.14 resolves the C2 branch of the supervised-auto activation sequence as CLOSE-BEFORE-ACTIVATION (R134); activation (am.12 R131/R132) resumes only after this task; M2-T015/T016 remain held (R143).
inputs: project-control/reports/M0-T046-g5-security.md (C2/M-1 finding: operator-named digest covers only the S13.5 instruction envelope, cli.py:1678/loop.py:1712; byte anchor prompt_bytes_digest is journal-resident; two-field forgery forwards)

project-control/reports/M0-T046-dcv-final.md (R124 adjudication: FORWARDED-AT ephemeral stamp at codex_reviewer.py:684 makes parked bytes non-reproducible - the property this fix must remove or work around)
outputs: Deterministic cryptographic binding of forwarded content to information covered by the operator-named approval_digest (design per R137: e.g. FORWARDED-AT injected only at actual forward time, or structured instruction persisted/recomputed at approve/resume)
R138 7-property adversarial test + R139 four also-prove tests
acceptance_scenarios: AS-1 (primary adversarial, R136/R138 - the verbatim owner test): park an authentic approval; mutate BOTH prompt and prompt_bytes_digest consistently in the journal; leave the operator-named approval digest unchanged; attempt approval/resume; it FAILS CLOSED; provider calls == 0; the refusal is durably/auditably recorded (sealed hash-chained audit event). Executable and non-vacuous (must fail on the pre-fix code).
AS-2 (R139a): the ordinary happy path still forwards exactly once, and the forwarded bytes verify against the binding derived from the operator-named approval digest.
AS-3 (R137/R139b): clock-only differences do NOT invalidate the operator's approval - the S13.5 'change only the clock and the approval does not change' invariant is preserved by an executable test.
AS-4 (R139c): post-approval tampering of the journal still refuses fail-closed at resume.

AS-5 (R139d/R140 prohibition): no SHADOW/supervised/limited-auto authority change; no forwarding-guard, activation-flag, or tier change; diff confined to allowed_paths; no redesign/features/infrastructure/cleanup beyond the single bounded fix.

AS-6 (negative/degenerate): a record missing the new binding material (old-shape park) refuses fail-closed rather than falling back to journal-resident-only verification; malformed/absent binding inputs refuse with distinct honest reason codes.
risks: The binding must be deterministic: any residual non-reproducible content in the parked bytes (beyond the clock) breaks the recompute/verify path - the producer must inventory build_forwarded_prompt inputs and either derive them from approval-covered material or move them to forward time.
Backward shape: pre-fix parked records lack the new binding material; they must refuse (AS-6), never silently fall back to the journal-resident anchor.
Keep the M0-T046 anchor checks intact or strictly strengthened - no weakening of tamper-before/after coverage while re-anchoring.
